query: For the paper "360{\deg} Stance Detection" (arXiv: 1804.00982), answer this question: what dataset did they use for this tool?
context:
[1] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
Stance detection is the task of estimating whether the attitude expressed in a text towards a given topic is ‘in favour’, ‘against’, or ‘neutral’. We collected and annotated a novel dataset, which associates news articles with a stance towards a speciﬁed topic. We then trained a state-of-the-art stance detection model (Augenstein et al., 2016) on this dataset. The stance detection model is integrated into the 360° Stance Detection website as a web service.

[2] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
360° Stance Detection Sebastian Ruder, John Glover, Afshin Mehrabani, Parsa Ghaffari Aylien Ltd., Dublin, Ireland {sebastian,john,afshin,parsa}@aylien.com Abstract The proliferation of fake news and ﬁlter bub- bles makes it increasingly difﬁcult to form an arXiv:1804.00982v1 [cs.CL] 3 Apr 2018 unbiased, balanced opinion towards a topic. To ameliorate this, we propose 360° Stance Detection, a tool that aggregates news with multiple perspectives on a topic.

Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
Science 376(12):86. William Ferreira and Andreas Vlachos. 2016. Emer- gent: a novel data-set for stance classiﬁcation. In Proceedings of the 2016 conference of the North American chapter of the association for computa- tional linguistics: Human language technologies. pages 1163–1168. Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, and Kilian Q. Wein- berger. 2017. On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks. Proceedings of ICML 2017 http:// arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599. Kazi Saidul Hasan and Vincent Ng.

[4] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
The stance detection model is exposed as a web service and returns for each article-target entity pair a stance label (i.e. one of ‘in favour’, ‘against’ or ‘neutral’) along with a probability.6 The demo then visualizes the collected news ar- ticles as a 2D scatter plot with each (x,y) coordi- nate representing a single news article from a par- ticular outlet that matched the user query. The x- axis shows the stance of the article in the range [−1, 1].

[5] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 5 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
Springer, pages 153–160. Marilyn A Walker, Pranav Anand, Robert Abbott, and Ricky Grant. 2012. Stance classiﬁcation using dia- logic properties of persuasion. In Proceedings of the In 2012 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Hu- man Language Technologies. Association for Com- putational Linguistics, pages 592–596. William Yang Wang. 2017. ”Liar , Liar Pants on Fire”: A New Benchmark Dataset for Fake News Detec- tion.

[6] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 3 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
4 Model We train a Bidirectional Encoding model (Augen- stein et al., 2016), which has achieved state-of- the-art results for Twitter stance detection on our dataset. The model encodes the entity using a bidi- rectional LSTM (BiLSTM)4, which is then used to initialize a BiLSTM that encodes the article and produces a prediction. To reduce the sequence length, we use the same context window that was presented to annotators for training the LSTM.

[7] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
360° Stance Detection is particularly useful to gain an overview of complex or controversial top- ics and to highlight differences in their perception across different outlets. We show visualizations for example queries and three controversial top- ics in Figure 3. By extending the tool to enable retrieval of a larger number of news articles and more ﬁne-grained ﬁltering, we can employ it for general news analysis.

[8] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
We hope that this tool will demonstrate how NLP can be used to help combat ﬁlter bubbles and fake news and to aid users in obtaining evidence on which they can base their opinions.

[9] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
6 Conclusion We have introduced 360° Stance Detection, a tool that aims to provide evidence and context in order to assist the user with forming a balanced opinion towards a controversial topic. It aggregates news with multiple perspectives on a topic, annotates them with their stance, and visualizes them on a spectrum ranging from support to opposition, al- lowing the user to skim excerpts of the articles or read the original source.

[10] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
A better alternative would be to provide addi- tional evidence that will allow a user to evaluate multiple viewpoints and decide with which they agree. To this end, we propose 360° Stance De- tection, a tool that provides a wide view of a topic from different perspectives to aid with forming a balanced opinion.

[11] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
Given a topic, the tool aggre- gates relevant news articles from different sources and leverages recent advances in stance detection to lay them out on a spectrum ranging from sup- port to opposition to the topic.

[12] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
Given a news search query and a topic, the tool retrieves news articles matching the query and an- alyzes their stance towards the topic.

[13] Source: 1804.00982.pdf | Page: 1 | Section: None
Title: 360{\deg} Stance Detection
The demo then visualizes the articles as a 2D scatter plot on a spectrum ranging from ‘against’ to ‘in favour’ weighted by the prominence of the news outlet and provides additional links and article excerpts as context.1 The interface allows the user to obtain an overview of the range of opinion that is exhib- ited towards a topic of interest by various news outlets.
